claims.claim: Math is not morally neutral in the deep structure of the thesis.
claims.plain_english: Mathematics carries moral meaning, not just numbers and formulas.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts this as a core claim of the thesis, supported by the structure of nineteen irreducible proofs and five core arguments.
claims.what_would_break_it: If mathematics could be shown to be entirely value-free and independent of any moral framework, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The moral claim is carried by structure, not slogan.
claims.plain_english: The moral meaning comes from how the arguments are built, not from catchy phrases.
claims.evidence_given: The document repeats this phrase as a key insight and positions it as the synthesis of the five core arguments.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the moral content could be reduced to a simple statement without relying on the structure of the proofs, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: There are nineteen irreducible proofs that together establish the moral nature of mathematics.
claims.plain_english: There are nineteen basic proofs that show math has a moral side.
claims.evidence_given: The document references nineteen irreducible proofs but does not list or explain them in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the nineteen proofs could be reduced to fewer or if they failed to connect to morality, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The five core arguments are the load-bearing structure of the thesis.
claims.plain_english: The five main arguments hold up the entire thesis.
claims.evidence_given: The document names the five core arguments as the structure before asking the reader to follow the full derivation.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the thesis could stand without these five arguments or if they were not logically connected, this claim would be false.
